title: Using Claude for Code
description: Harness Claude's long context and strong reasoning for complex coding tasks, large file analysis, and architectural decisions.

data.text: Claude, developed by Anthropic, has become the favorite coding model for many developers. Claude 3.5 Sonnet in particular is widely regarded as the best general-purpose coding model available. Its strengths include an exceptionally large context window, strong instruction-following, and a clean, readable code style that closely matches human-written code.

Claude offers one of the largest context windows available — up to 200,000 tokens in Claude 3. That is roughly 150,000 words, or dozens of source files. For coding, this means you can paste a much larger portion of your codebase into the prompt and Claude can reason about the whole thing at once. This is a major advantage over models with smaller context windows.

data.title: Use the context window for cross-file understanding
data.text: Paste multiple related files into Claude to give it cross-file context. If you are refactoring a data flow that spans a controller, a service, and a model, paste all three. Claude can reason about how they interact and suggest changes that preserve the overall architecture.

Claude's Artifacts feature generates complete, runnable files or mini-applications in a side panel. You can see the full code, edit it, and run it in some interfaces. This is ideal for prototyping data transformations, HTML/CSS components, small utilities, or even full micro-applications before porting them into your project.
Best Use Cases for Claude in Development

data.title: Where Claude excels:
items: Analyzing large files or multiple files at once
Architectural decisions that require understanding the full system
Refactoring complex code while preserving behavior
Writing clean, well-commented code that follows best practices

data.text: Claude in the IDE via Cursor

Cursor lets you use Claude as the underlying model for Chat and Composer. This gives you the best of both worlds: Claude's reasoning power combined with Cursor's codebase awareness. To switch, open Cursor settings, navigate to Models, and select Claude as the default chat and composer model.

Claude responds very well to detailed, structured prompts. You can give it multi-paragraph instructions, specify exact requirements, and even provide style guides. It follows complex instructions better than most other models. Use this to your advantage by being thorough in your prompts.

data.title: Effective Claude prompt for refactoring
data.content:
"I have a 200-line function in src/utils/dataProcessor.ts that handles data transformation. It is difficult to test and has several nested callbacks. Please:
1. Analyze the function and identify the distinct responsibilities
2. Propose a refactored structure with separate functions
3. Write the refactored code preserving exact behavior
4. Add JSDoc comments to each function explaining its purpose
5. Ensure all error handling is preserved

Use our project's existing patterns in src/utils/ as a style reference."

data.text: Claude vs. Other Models for Code

For most coding tasks, Claude 3.5 Sonnet is the strongest choice. It produces cleaner code, follows instructions more precisely, and handles larger context windows better than GPT-4 or earlier Claude models. GPT-4 is still useful for data tasks and when you need Code Interpreter. For day-to-day coding, Claude has become the default choice for many professional developers.

In the Claude API or Claude.ai interface, you can set a system prompt that applies to the entire conversation. For coding sessions, a system prompt like 'You are a senior developer who writes clean, well-tested code. Always explain your reasoning before writing code. Follow the project's existing patterns and conventions.' gives Claude a consistent quality bar across all responses.

data.title: Claude in your IDE
data.text: For the best experience, use Claude inside Cursor rather than copy-pasting between Claude.ai and your editor. Cursor's codebase indexing means Claude has access to your project structure without you pasting files manually.
